title: Adaptive burn-rate SLOs and paging policy overhaul for observability platform
creator: Marco Chen
description: Problem: Our current SLO alerting is based primarily on simple threshold rules (p95 latency > X or error rate > Y) which leads to two issues: noisy pagers from short-lived spikes, and lack of correlation between alerting signals and real customer impact. We do not currently have burn-rate logic wired into paging policies, and anomaly detection is siloed from our burn-rate calculations. This ticket implements an end-to-end improvement: compute burn-rate SLI windows from the metrics/log pipeline, add adaptive burn-rate evaluation, surface burn-rate-derived alerts in dashboards, and drive paging/escalation policy decisions with burn-rate + anomaly signals. We will also enhance tracing hooks so on-call can quickly jump from a burn-rate alert to representative traces and sampled spans to accelerate RCA. Goals: 1) Reduce noisy pages from transient bursts while maintaining high sensitivity to sustained reliability regressions. 2) Enable deterministic, auditable paging rules tied to SLO budgets. 3) Provide on-call context: representative traces, top-error traces, service-level rollups, and a timeline of metrics and logs. 4) Integrate anomaly detection to reduce false negatives on subtle degradations.
acceptance_criteria: Burn-rate computation runs in near-real-time (<= 60s pipeline delay) for core inference SLOs (text-gen, embeddings, chat).
Two configurable burn-rate windows implemented (short: 5m, medium: 1h) with parameterized multipliers for budget consumption.
Pager rules: page on short-window burn-rate >= 3 OR medium-window burn-rate >= 1.5 when customer-impact tagged as high.
Anomaly detector scores integrated to suppress pages when burn-rate is driven by synthetic load or known maintenance windows (configurable).
Tracing hook added: the alert payload includes direct links to sampled traces and representative spans for the affected service and model.
Dashboards updated: per-service SLO burn-rate chart, per-customer burn-rate heatmap, alert timeline, and top contributing error logs.
On-call runbook updated with clear escalation steps, runbook links, and playbooks for common failure modes.
Automated tests: unit tests for burn-rate math, e2e test that fires synthetic load and verifies page behavior, and smoke checks for trace-link generation.
implementation_notes: Metrics pipeline: add a pre-aggregation step in metrics ETL to emit rolling-window budget consumption at 10s granularity for top-level SLIs.
Logs: ensure request_id propagation from gateway to runtime to make tracing links for sampled spans reliable.
Compute: implement burn-rate evaluator as an internal service (k8s deployment) with a small in-memory sliding-window optimized for constant time updates.
Policy engine: extend existing alerting-policy service to accept burn-rate signals and anomaly-suppression metadata; add feature-flag gating for canary rollout.
Anomaly detection: prototype using z-score on rate-normalized error counts then evaluate replacing with short LSTM model in follow-up ticket if precision insufficient.
Dashboarding: add a combined SLO timeline panel in Console with links to logs and traces; create a compact 'pager' view for on-call mobile notifications.
